_readme.purpose: Ordered claim scenarios for the live hackathon demo recording. Submit in the exact order given — several scenarios only produce their intended flag because of claims submitted earlier in this same sequence (e.g., scenario 5 only shows 'repeat_claimant' because scenarios 3 and 4 already exist).
_readme.prerequisite: Run demo_assets/seed_statistical_baseline.py FIRST, before submitting any of these — it pre-loads 32 baseline claims so the Statistical Agent's sample-size thresholds are already met when scenario 9 (the outlier) is submitted.
_readme.important_limitation: Scenarios relying on Gemini's EXTRACTED fields (incident_date, claimed_amount) — specifically scenarios 8 and 9 — can only be verified correctly with a REAL GEMINI_API_KEY set. In MOCK_MODE (no key), extraction always returns the same fixed canned values regardless of input text, so these two scenarios will NOT show their intended behavior until tested against real Gemini. Scenarios 1-7 rely only on raw input fields (claimant_id, address, policy_number, raw_text) which work identically in mock or real mode.
_readme.evidence_images_location: demo_assets/images/ — all clearly labeled placeholder illustrations (see file header comments in generate_images.py), not real photographs. Gemini's real vision capability reads the embedded text and reasons about it genuinely.
_readme.recommended_video_usage: Scenarios 1 and 2 make the best on-camera 'live submission' moments (clean vs. flagged, side by side). Scenarios 3-7 are better pre-submitted before recording (via submit_demo_scenarios.py) so their pattern relationships already exist when you show scenario 7's result. Scenario 9 (the outlier) is a strong closing moment if submitted live after the baseline is seeded.

scenarios.raw_text: On July 2, 2026, my car was scraped in a parking lot at low speed. The rear bumper has a minor scratch and paint transfer. Repair estimate is 4500 rupees.
scenarios.expected_consistency: None — narrative matches evidence (both describe minor cosmetic damage)
scenarios.expected_statistical_flags: None (amount too small/typical to register as an outlier)
scenarios.presenter_note: Use this first to establish the baseline 'this is what a normal, fast-approved claim looks like' before showing the flagged one.

scenarios.scenario_name: HIGH severity consistency mismatch — flagship demo moment
scenarios.raw_text: On July 20, 2026, I was in a major front-end collision. The car is undrivable with extensive structural damage requiring full panel replacement. Repair estimate is 185000 rupees.
scenarios.expected_consistency: HIGH severity — narrative describes major structural damage; the paired image (deliberately mismatched) shows only a minor cosmetic scuff
scenarios.expected_pattern_flags: shared_address_ring will begin building once scenarios 6/7 (same address) are also submitted
scenarios.expected_statistical_flags: None yet (single high-value claim, but Isolation Forest needs the baseline first — run the seed script before this)
scenarios.presenter_note: THE key moment of the video. Narrate: 'Watch the Consistency Agent catch this' as the flag appears with its specific reasoning text.

scenarios.scenario_name: Duplicate submission — exact resubmission of scenario 2
scenarios.raw_text: On July 20, 2026, I was in a major front-end collision. The car is undrivable with extensive structural damage requiring full panel replacement. Repair estimate is 185000 rupees.
scenarios.expected_consistency: Same HIGH severity mismatch as scenario 2 (independently re-evaluated)
scenarios.expected_pattern_flags: duplicate_submission — identical policy_number + identical raw_text as scenario 2
scenarios.expected_overall: flagged, high risk (compounded by duplicate flag)
scenarios.presenter_note: Good for showing the Pattern Agent catches EXACT resubmission independent of the Consistency Agent's own (separate) finding.

scenarios.raw_text: On March 10, 2026, minor rear bumper damage from a parking collision. Repair estimate is 8500 rupees.
scenarios.expected_pattern_flags: None yet (first claim from this claimant)
scenarios.presenter_note: Submit before recording — this and scenarios 5, 6 build the history for the repeat_claimant flag.

scenarios.raw_text: On May 2, 2026, side mirror damage from a street scrape. Repair estimate is 3200 rupees.
scenarios.presenter_note: Submit before recording, same as scenario 4.

scenarios.scenario_name: Repeat claimant, part 3 of 3 — THIS ONE should show the flag
scenarios.raw_text: On July 19, 2026, a windshield chip from road debris. Repair estimate is 4100 rupees.
scenarios.expected_pattern_flags: repeat_claimant — 2 prior claims from CL-DEMO-003 now on file
scenarios.expected_overall: flagged (medium — pattern flag on an otherwise clean-looking claim)
scenarios.presenter_note: Can be submitted LIVE on camera since scenarios 4/5 already established the history — a good 'each individual claim looks fine, but the pattern doesn't' moment.

scenarios.scenario_name: Shared address ring, part 1 of 2 (pairs with scenario 2's address)
scenarios.raw_text: On June 28, 2026, side panel dent from a parking mishap. Repair estimate is 15000 rupees.
scenarios.expected_pattern_flags: shared_address_ring — same address as scenario 2's claimant (different claimant_id)
scenarios.presenter_note: Submit after scenario 2 — this is what turns scenario 2's claim into a COMPOUND example (both consistency AND pattern flags) if you re-check scenario 2's claim afterward, since the ring is now 2 claimants strong at that address.

scenarios.scenario_name: Policy-date anomaly — REQUIRES real Gemini to verify
scenarios.raw_text: The incident happened on July 5, 2026 — front bumper and headlight damage from a collision. Repair estimate is 32000 rupees.
scenarios.expected_pattern_flags: policy_date_anomaly — narrative states incident date (July 5) is 5 days BEFORE the policy_start_date field (July 10)
scenarios.presenter_note: IMPORTANT: this only works if Gemini correctly extracts 'July 5, 2026' as the incident_date from the narrative text. Verify this with a real API key before recording — do not assume it works from mock-mode testing.

scenarios.scenario_name: Extreme outlier — Isolation Forest, REQUIRES real Gemini + baseline seeded first
scenarios.raw_text: My vehicle was stolen from a secured parking garage overnight on July 1, 2026. Police FIR is attached. The vehicle's insured value and claim amount is 550000 rupees.
scenarios.expected_consistency: None — narrative and evidence (police FIR) are consistent; this is a DELIBERATELY clean, high-value claim
scenarios.expected_statistical_flags: isolation_forest_outlier — 550000 stands far outside the seeded baseline's typical range (1200-9200), ONLY IF demo_assets/seed_statistical_baseline.py was run first
scenarios.expected_overall: flagged on statistical grounds alone, despite being a fully consistent, well-documented claim
scenarios.presenter_note: Strong closing scenario: narrate that this proves the system doesn't just flag inconsistent evidence — it also catches statistical outliers even when everything else checks out, which is a distinct and complementary detection mechanism. Requires the baseline seed script run first AND a real Gemini key for the 550000 figure to be extracted correctly.
